name: KAM
spec: ECMA-48 §7.2.11; refused: a program could lock the keyboard of the only terminal on the console

name: BDSM
spec: ECMA-48 §7.2.1, the Terminal Working Group's BiDi recommendation: set, the cursor's paragraph (the rows a wrap joins) is in implicit mode, reset in explicit mode; SM and RM set the current value, which each new paragraph takes, and mark the cursor's paragraph when the cursor stands at its first position; in a build with the bidi feature, and a build without it has no such row, so DECRQM answers 0

name: DCSM
spec: ECMA-48 §7.2.3; permanently set: editing always acts on the data, the order the program wrote; in a build with the bidi feature, and a build without it has no such row, so DECRQM answers 0

name: SRM
spec: ECMA-48 §7.2.15; reset, what the terminal sends the program is also shown (local echo)

name: LNM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; kept though ECMA-48's 5th edition withdraws it

name: DECCKM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510

name: DECANM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; VT52 is declined for now ([the VT52 issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/65)), so DECRQM reports ANSI mode as permanent

name: DECCOLM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; refused: the console's size comes from the display and the font

name: DECSCLM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; a console has no smooth scroll

name: DECSCNM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510

name: DECOM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; the cursor goes home as it is set or reset (VT100 User Guide)

name: DECAWM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510

name: DECARM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; the host repeats a held key, and stops while it is reset

name: X10MOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, X10 mouse; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: CURBLINK
default: set by the host's cursor blink
spec: ctlseqs, AT&T 610 cursor blink; held in a DECSCUSR style, while the default style blinks as the host's setting says

name: DECPFF
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; a console has no printer

name: DECPEX
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; a console has no printer

name: DECTCEM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510

name: DECNRCM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; refused: national replacement sets are obsolete next to UTF-8

name: ALLOW80TO132
spec: ctlseqs; DECCOLM is refused, so 80 to 132 columns is never allowed

name: XTREVWRAP
spec: ctlseqs, reverse wraparound: while DECAWM is set, BS and CUB go on from the first column to the last column of the row above when printing wrapped from that row, as xterm moves; a pending wrap takes one step, so CUB n from it ends n - 1 columns left of the last column, where xterm's CursorBack counts the pending wrap twice for n of 2 or more and ends n - 2 columns left

name: ALTBUF
spec: ctlseqs, the alternate screen, neither cleared nor the cursor saved

name: DECNKM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; the keypad's application mode, which DECKPAM sets and DECKPNM resets

name: DECLRMM
spec: ctlseqs; VT510; set, `CSI Pl ; Pr s` is DECSLRM and sets the left and right margins, and `CSI s` with no parameter sets them to the whole width; reset, the margins are the whole width and `CSI s` is SCOSC

name: DECSDM
spec: ctlseqs, DECSDM in xterm's sense: set, sixel scrolling is off and a picture sits at the screen's top left, cut to the screen, with the cursor left where it is; reset, a picture's top left is the cursor's cell

name: VT200MOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, normal tracking; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: HILITEMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs; refused: the terminal waits on the program's XTHIMOUSE answer before it can show a selection

name: BTNMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, button-event tracking; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: ANYMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, any-event tracking; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: FOCUS
spec: ctlseqs, FocusIn and FocusOut; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: SGRMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, SGR encoding, whatever order the modes were set in; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: UTF8MOUSE
spec: ctlseqs; never on: SGR mouse (1006) replaces the UTF-8 encoding

name: ALTSCROLL
spec: ctlseqs, alternate scroll: on the alternate screen, while no tracking mode is set, a wheel step the host does not report is sent as cursor-up or cursor-down keys, one a line, as DECCKM encodes them; set at start, as foot and Ghostty start it

name: URXVTMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, urxvt encoding: CSI Cb ; Cx ; Cy M in decimal, Cb as the X10 encoding's byte and the cell counted from 1, with no limit; one encoding at a time, as 1006; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: PIXMOUSE
spec: ctlseqs, SGR-Pixels encoding, pixels counted from 1; DECSTR resets it, where xterm resets it on RIS only

name: SCROLLTTYOUTPUT
spec: ctlseqs, rxvt; never on: the view stays where it is while output arrives

name: SCROLLKEY
spec: ctlseqs, rxvt; always on: a key press scrolls the view back to the bottom

name: META8BIT
spec: ctlseqs, eightBitInput: while 1036 is reset, Alt sets the eighth bit of a key that sends one byte below 0x80, sent as U+0080 to U+00FF in the input's encoding; neither set, Alt sends nothing of its own

name: NUMLOCK
spec: ctlseqs, numLock: while NumLock is on, a keypad key that makes a character sends it whatever DECKPAM says; set at start, as xterm's numLock resource; vtium has one Alt modifier, so the mode changes only how NumLock reads

name: METAESC
spec: ctlseqs, metaSendsEscape: Alt puts ESC before a key's bytes; set at start, so Alt with a key works as Meta in shells and editors without the program asking

name: BELL
spec: ctlseqs, bellIsUrgent; vtium has no window to mark urgent, so set lets BEL reach the host, which rings the VT bell by its bell setting, and reset BEL does nothing; set at start, so a program's BEL rings the VT bell without the program asking

name: TITEINHIBIT
spec: ctlseqs; always on: the alternate screen is always allowed

name: ALTBUF1047
spec: ctlseqs, the alternate screen, cleared as it is left

name: SAVECUR
spec: ctlseqs, "Save cursor as in DECSC": set saves, reset restores as DECRC does, and nothing stays set

name: ALTBUF1049
spec: ctlseqs, the cursor saved as in DECSC and the alternate screen cleared as it is entered; leaving restores the cursor and the pen as DECRC does

name: SIXELPRIVATE
spec: ctlseqs, private sixel color registers: set, each picture starts from the default registers; reset, the pictures share one set of registers, kept until RIS or a change of the register count

name: BIDIARROWS
spec: the Terminal Working Group's BiDi recommendation, as mintty documents it: set, the Left and Right arrow keys swap while the cursor's paragraph resolves right to left; in a build with the bidi feature, and a build without it has no such row, so DECRQM answers 0

name: BRPASTE
spec: ctlseqs, bracketed paste; a paste never carries its own end marker

name: SYNC
spec: contour synchronized-output; offered while the host presents by it

name: GRAPHEME
default: set by the host's width method
spec: contour unicode-core; RIS and DECSTR return it to the configured method

name: REFLOW
spec: contour line-reflow-mode; each print, and SM and RM on the cursor's row, mark a row as rewrapping at a width change or, reset, cut at a narrower margin; RIS sets it

name: SCHEMEREPORT
spec: contour color-palette-update-notifications; CSI ? 997 ; Ps n when the default background turns dark or light by its luma (ITU-R BT.601), as CSI ? 996 n answers

name: VISREPORT
spec: foot(7), rockorager's visibility reports; CSI ? 999 ; Ps n as it is set and on each change, a VT switch or a blank

name: RESIZEREPORT
spec: rockorager's in-band resize notifications; CSI 48 ; rows ; cols ; height ; width t as it is set and after each resize, the text area in pixels 0 while the cell size is unknown

name: BIDIBOX
spec: the Terminal Working Group's BiDi recommendation, as mintty documents it: set, box drawing in a right-to-left paragraph draws mirrored; SM and RM set the current value, which each new paragraph takes, and mark the cursor's paragraph when the cursor stands at its first position; in a build with the bidi feature, and a build without it has no such row, so DECRQM answers 0

name: BIDIAUTO
spec: the Terminal Working Group's BiDi recommendation, as mintty documents it: set, each paragraph's direction is detected from its first strong character; SM and RM set the current value, which each new paragraph takes, and mark the cursor's paragraph when the cursor stands at its first position, and DECSTR and RIS return it to vtium.conf's `text-direction`, set under `auto`; in a build with the bidi feature, and a build without it has no such row, so DECRQM answers 0

name: SIXELRIGHT
spec: ctlseqs, sixel cursor to the right: set, the cursor ends a picture in the column after its right edge, at most the last column; reset, at its left column
